text: Nobody moves. Sora holds the end of the bridge, and the team behind her is frozen.
She doesn't even turn her head. One move from the ledge, and she shoots the Operator.
On her wrist, the compass trembles between two pulses. Its needle hunts summons in field form.
Jaeha watches her wrist, not the bolt, and sees it: she never looks back. The needle does her looking.
Moon Ahin warns him how good Sora is. He knows. He's watched her since Gate 0912.
Nib creeps one step left. The needle snaps left, and without looking, Sora shoots the tip off his scarf.
Lyra draws. The needle snaps right, and Sora splits Lyra's arrow on the string, again without looking.
She reloads with one flick. Why look behind her, darling, when the compass does it for her?
One minute thirty-one, and the rim narrows another notch.
Her orders say alive. She feels that leaves her a lot of room.
Jaeha has found her habit, like every boss's: she trusts the needle. So he'll move it.
Through Link, three silent orders go out at once: a decoy, a shield, and an archer waiting for thunder.
Borro flares back into field form in front of Lyra. A new, stronger pulse.
The needle swings right, then snaps back left.
Because Nib explodes off the ledge at her left, knives drawn: the closest pulse she has.
Sora spins left after the needle.
Mid-leap, Jaeha drops Nib into rest form, invisible to the compass. Nib falls flat behind Number One.
With the left pulse gone, the needle swings right, to the two bright pulses there.
Sora spins after it, loads a heavy core-tipped bolt, and fires where the needle points.
Straight into Borro's shield, in a burst of violet light. Behind him, Lyra nocks an arrow.
Jaeha passes the blow through his body, Borro to Lyra, losing thirty percent. Blood bursts from his nose.
Moon Ahin has been paying attention too. One tiny flick of the baton at the far end.
Number One lets go of the stump with one hand and clamps it round Sora's ankle.
Borrowed Thunder, part two: Lyra's arrow leaves with the boom of Sora's own bolt behind it.
It hits the compass, not Sora. The brass shatters, and the needle spins away into the abyss.
Sora stares at her bare wrist, just a thin red line where the chain was.
Then she laughs, delighted. Director Baek is going to love him, she says again. It sounds like a warning.
She twists free, flips onto the ledge, and is gone through the side door, still laughing.
Lyra is furious: she had Sora's heart and took the compass. Jaeha thanks her for exactly that.
Another husk falls. Fifty-eight seconds.
Moon Ahin half carries Jaeha the last few metres, cracks running under every step.
Borro scoops them onto the ledge, and the white threads snap loose from Jaeha one by one.
Moon Ahin calls them home, all twenty-eight, and the bridge folds up onto the ledge, Number One last.
The rim is down to a slit a metre wide.
Borro jams his shield into the gap and heaves the iris plates apart with his back.
All night, Kanghan has shut doors on people. Borro holds this one open and roars at them to go.
The crew squeeze through into the white, pushing and pulling each other.
Twenty-eight husks pour through two by two, faster than they've ever moved.
Borro's arms tremble. Twelve seconds.
Lyra dives through, then Nib. Moon Ahin stops in the gap and looks back.
Jaeha stumbles and nearly falls. Moon Ahin shouts for him by his number.
She hauls him into the white by the wrist, and Borro dives after them as the iris slams shut.
Then darkness, and the count hits zero.
They tumble out onto the riverbank mud in one heap. Behind them, the gate is a dark steel plate.
The crew lie on their backs under the orange lights. Pyo laughs without a sound. The brothers hold each other.
Moon Ahin sits up in the mud and counts her husks, the way Jaeha counts people. Number One included.
But Jaeha lies face down. Nib shakes him and throws his rule back at him: everyone came back, so he has to.
One eye opens, and naturally, his first question is the head count.
Nib nods fast, eyes wet. All of them. For once, the count includes husks.
Torch beams run at them, and police lights come flashing down the riverside road.
Moon Ahin stands up between the guards and the team. Kanghan's heir has picked a side, and explains it to the guards in terms of their arms.
The guards skid to a stop and look at each other.
Jaeha rolls over and fumbles out his phone. He promised Seoa dinner at seven. She should know he's coming.
Seoa has been asking if he's alive since half past two. His thumb manages one letter: o.
His thumb jerks over the screen. It can't land on a key.
The phone slips out of his hands into the mud.
He holds his hands up against the bridge lights. They shake so hard they blur.
For the first time tonight, Jaeha can't read the trap. It's his own hands.
The phone buzzes beside his head. Seoa wants to know what o means. He can't even pick it up.
